field.whereRequired: A filter is required — to touch every record, say so explicitly in the condition

help.where:
Which records to take. An object: table field name → value or condition.
Empty — every record.

`{ maxId: user.id }` — maxId equals user.id
`{ age: { gt: 18 } }` — greater than 18 (also gte, lt, lte, ne)
`{ status: { in: ['new', 'open'] } }` — one of the values (notIn — none of them)
`{ name: { contains: 'Iv' } }` — text contains (also startsWith, like, ilike)
`{ phone: { isNull: true } }` — the field is empty
`{ maxId: user.id, gone: false }` — all conditions at once
`{ or: [{ status: 'new' }, { status: 'open' }] }` — any of the conditions

Written as a JavaScript object: not `maxId = user.id` but `{ maxId: user.id }`.
Quote a field name with a space or a dash: `{ 'order date': { gte: '2026-01-01' } }`.
id, createdAt and updatedAt are available too.
help.whereRequired:
Which records to touch — required.
`{ id: record.id }` — one record
`{ status: 'new', age: { lt: 18 } }` — by conditions, same syntax as in “Select records”
`{ id: record.id, version: record.version }` — only if nobody changed the record since it was read
Every record — only explicitly: `{ id: { isNull: false } }`.
help.orderBy:
Comma-separated field names, each optionally asc (default) or desc.
`name`
`createdAt desc`
`status asc, createdAt desc`
Empty — in insertion order.
help.limit: How many records to return: 100 by default, at most 1000.
help.offset: How many leading records to skip — for paging: `0`, `100`, `200`…
help.id: The record id (a string), e.g. `record.id` from another action's result.
help.row:
An object: field name → value.
`{ maxId: user.id, created: new Date().toISOString(), joined: true }`
The table's required fields must be set.
help.set:
An object with only the fields that change.
`{ gone: true }`
`{ status: 'done', attempts: record.attempts + 1 }`
